findings: Actual registered trader factories create TraderJob and set exact factoryId through SpiritJobFactory.create. Saved spiritJob goes through registry factory then reader. Invalid identifier/unknown registry .orElseThrow is not locally recovered.

Fresh job currentRecipe empty; first nonempty main-hand selection always sets conversionTimer=0, discarding restored partial timer even for valid matching recipe. Only source reload behavior, no native runtime proof.

Main-hand is not merely assumed vanilla equipment: SpiritEntity overrides getItemBySlot/setItemSlot to its resource inventory slot0; whole inventory explicitly serialized/deserialized. Same-version native getItemInHand bridge and transfer library serialization internals not in this source cache review, so no universal native equipment claim.

Codec requires trader_id STRING, no optional default. Normal source datagen stone_to_otherstone builds stones ingredient -> two OTHERSTONE items weight1 exact occultism:trader_otherstone. Builder creates actual SpiritTradeRecipe with factory string. This is datagen source, not proof generated current-pack recipe JSON or registry runtime loaded. update null-trader allowance is effectively excluded by this matches() nonnull input trader equality, although programmatically null onInit would still throw.

Factory suppliers pass configuration operationTimer directly. Default otherstone/otherrock10 count4, sapling20 count1, gambler200 count16. aiStep increments conversion once per loaded server update without seconds conversion; getTimeToConvert seconds comment is misleading, source does not implement seconds here. Missing saved maxTradesPerRound=0 disables loop and timeToConvert=0 matures every matched update; persisted values bypass config reader ranges.

At threshold resets counter then each chosen result copies full source ItemStack, copies entire pre-shrink input for event, shrinks input1 and writes slot before onConvert/event/output. No escrow or atomic debit-and-deliver receipt. Input event copy may count >1 although actual payment1; downstream event handlers not read.

ItemTransferUtil.insertItemStacked opens/commits transaction for insertion and returns copied remainder. TraderJob ignores returned remainder and sets flag=false whenever handler exists. If handler accepts less than full output, no fallback drop/escrow remains in this caller. Capacity failure thus has concrete static unhandled remainder; actual full-inventory scenario not executed, foreign transfer implementation exceptions/cancellation not audited. Library insertion transaction does not include prior input debit.

PickupItemsGoal instead explicitly applies returned remainder to original ItemEntity after simulated/actual insertion. No no-loss universal claim: concurrent changes and serializer semantics untested. No recipe branch empties slot before spawning refund with unchecked null; delivery failure is not restored.

Paid trader partial-time reset and unhandled output remainder support migration/task-integration design boundaries, but generic paid process/custody variants are already represented. No new semantic owner accepted, no alternate candidate invented.
application_to_existing_quest_system: Do not treat a saved progress field as verified resumed work without checking first-update cache reconstruction.
Payment and output insertion must have an actual native receipt; a failed output insertion cannot mark quest delivery complete.
Keep full item/components and paid-count identity; do not equate copied whole input event payload to quantity actually paid.
